props.title: Angrezi Medium

sections.content: **Angrezi Medium** (2020) stands as Irrfan Khan's final completed film before his untimely death, delivering a touching exploration of father-daughter relationships and the aspirations of small-town India. The film follows the spiritual successor format of Hindi Medium (2017), though it tells an entirely new story. Khan's portrayal of Champak Bansal, a sweet shop owner determined to fulfill his daughter's dream of studying abroad, captures the emotional complexity of parent-child relationships in modernizing India, similar to themes explored in **Piku** (2015) and **Secret Superstar** (2017).

sections.content: The film particularly excels in depicting the cultural clash between traditional Indian values and Western education aspirations. Director Homi Adajania brings nuance to this familiar theme, avoiding the heavy-handed messaging seen in films like **3 Idiots** (2009). The chemistry between Irrfan Khan and Radhika Madan feels authentically strained yet loving, reminiscent of the father-daughter dynamic in **Dangal** (2016), though focused on academic rather than athletic ambitions.

Supporting performances by Deepak Dobriyal and Kareena Kapoor Khan add layers to the narrative, though the film occasionally struggles with pacing in its London sequences. The movie's strength lies in its authentic portrayal of Udaipur's small-town life, following in the footsteps of films like **Bareilly Ki Barfi** (2017) and **Sui Dhaaga** (2018) in celebrating the aspirations of non-metropolitan India. sections.content: **Angrezi Medium** joins a crucial conversation in Indian cinema about education and social mobility, alongside films like **Chalk N Duster** (2016) and **Hichki** (2018). The film's exploration of language as both barrier and bridge resonates with earlier works like English Vinglish (2012), though it takes a more contemporary approach to the challenges faced by Indian students seeking international education.
